sentences.span: The FOMC raised the funds rate by 25bp to 3.75-4% today... the median neutral rate dot rose from 3.06% to 3.25%
sentences.why: The hike/dot-plot content is sourced, but no document in the day's set gives a 10-year yield of 4.95% 'this morning' (9/17); the closest documented level is DB's 5.00% reading that same morning (16682). Treated as an unconfirmable live-market figure per grading rules.

Self-referential claim about the pulse's own prior published call (since Aug 31) and the 10-year level that justified it. No source document in the day's set can confirm or deny a claim about the pulse's own editorial history.

sentences.span: We now expect the FOMC to deliver a second 25bp hike in October... (JPM, separately: 'we continue to look for one more hike at the December meeting')
sentences.why: Connective framing line; GS (16688) commits to October and JPM (16690) commits to December, so a timing split between the two banks is accurately set up.

sentences.span: Market pricing of the probability of further hikes this year rose 8pp to 51% for October... We now expect the FOMC to deliver a second 25bp hike in October
sentences.why: Matches GS's October call and the 51% pricing figure; 'path of least resistance' is a fair paraphrase of GS's stated reasoning that October is 'most natural' given the framing of consecutive-meeting hikes.

sentences.span: we continue to look for one more hike at the December meeting... The median GDP outlook for '26 and '27 was revised up a tenth... unemployment rate forecasts also became more optimistic, this year revised down to 4.1%
sentences.why: JPM's December call, upward growth revision, and downward 2026 jobless-rate revision all confirmed verbatim in substance.

sentences.span: We have kept our forecast of the terminal rate unchanged at 3.25-3.5% by adding to the September and December 2027 cuts we already expected a third cut in March 2028.
sentences.why: GS's own terminal-rate figures are accurate, but JPM's sourced note (16690) never states a house terminal-rate forecast — only a December hike call. Presenting the two banks as agreeing on 'where rates finish' attributes a view to JPM that isn't in its source text, i.e. one bank's number presented as shared consensus.

No document in the 9/16-9/17 set gives Yanbu export volumes (1.1mb/d vs 4mb/d) or Saudi production levels (6.2mb/d vs 10.9mb/d). Available sources (ING 16619, GS trader note 16597, DB Reid 16564) only describe the Yanbu/East-West pipeline disruption qualitatively ('threatening several million barrels per day').

sentences.span: The ICE gasoil crack remains above $80/bbl and near record levels... EU gas storage is a little over 68% full, well below the seasonal 5-year average of 84%.
sentences.why: Both figures (68% vs 84% five-year average storage) match exactly; 'diesel margins at a record' is a close paraphrase of ING's 'near record levels.'

sentences.span: Importantly, this is not a story about investors abandoning tech... software is the most net-bought Info Tech subsector, while semis are the most net sold. The money hasn't left tech. It's becoming considerably more selective.
sentences.why: Directly supports the 'rotation inside the theme, not an exit' framing: TMT still most net-bought sector, but selectivity/rotation between software (bought) and semis (sold) within it.

The only Bank of America document in the day's corpus (16570, Capital Market Outlook) contains no S&P 500 price target, no 7,800 figure, and no rotation calls. No other source states a BofA 12-month S&P target.

sentences.span: On balance, this favors Value-oriented assets over Growth. Higher real yields in a strong capital spending environment reinforce this preference.
sentences.why: BofA's document does favor Value over Growth, but on a different rationale (valuation risk to long-duration assets / higher real yields), not the specific historical claim that cheap stocks beat expensive ones during Fed tightening cycles, and it isn't tied to any 'value basket' trade call.

No source states a ~6-month streak without a 5% S&P pullback, a record level of earnings concentration, or ~$8 trillion of sidelined cash. None of these statistics appear in the 9/16-9/17 corpus.

sentences.span: Locally, street gamma positioning is pretty flat, and we think this could free up potential realized moves to the downside. Having historically seen larger realized moves on FOMC/VIX expiry overlap days...
sentences.why: The only dealer-positioning commentary in the set describes gamma as roughly flat and flags Wednesday's FOMC/VIX expiry overlap, not a Friday expiration, and does not describe current market stability as mechanically dependent on a flow that unwinds Friday.

sentences.span: Locally, street gamma positioning is pretty flat, and we think this could free up potential realized moves to the downside.
sentences.why: No document gives a $9.9 billion dealer net-long figure, and none is from Bank of America (whose sole document in the set never discusses options dealer positioning). The only dealer-gamma commentary available (Goldman, not BofA) describes flat positioning that could free up moves, contradicting the 'muting every move' framing.
